public_rationale: The evidence supports inexpensive fake engagement and synthetic conversations that can deceive readers. It also documents effective removals on some platforms. These findings establish a real vulnerability, but do not settle the full cost-and-speed claim. Treating pennies as a per-interaction cost or moments as text-generation time would add measures the speaker did not supply.
limitations: This is not evidence that coordinated manipulation is expensive or harmless.
The conversation study tests reader deception, not live account creation or political persuasion.
The platform experiment primarily uses non-political scenarios.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that very cheap coordination and rapidly fabricated human-looking personas enable covert manipulation of public discussion.
‘Counterfeit a human identity’ means a plausible online persona, not necessarily a forged government identity.
‘Wide open’ means materially vulnerable, not that every attack succeeds or that defenses are absent.
Pennies and moments express low cost and short creation time, but cannot silently be converted into cost per token, per post, or per account.
This is a causal capability claim, not a deadline-bound forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Attack demonstrations or platform experiments connect low-cost coordinated accounts and rapidly created plausible personas to successful deceptive participation, amplification, or manipulation of public discussion.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Matched realistic tests show that these capabilities fail to provide the asserted access or manipulation opportunity, or that the claimed low-cost and rapid-creation combination is unavailable under the relevant conditions.

evidence.explanation: The report documents inexpensive purchased fake engagement and automated AI-content publishing, but also meaningful removals. It does not time the creation of credible identities or establish that an entire coordinated mob costs pennies.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A reproducible deployment study reporting swarm size, total and marginal costs, time to create usable human-looking identities, and actual deceptive reach or manipulation, under a clearly stated reading of pennies and moments.
